Financial markets expect the Reserve Bank will announce another interest rate hike on Tuesday, March 17, just six weeks after its first rate hike in more than two years. But markets are also anticipating a third hike from the RBA in May, at its third meeting of 2026. That would take the official cash rate back to 4.35 per cent, right where it was before the RBA started its cutting cycle in 2025. HSBC chief economist Paul Bloxham says Australia needs to have a downturn to solve its inflation problem. He says, the question is how deep it will be and how long it'll run. "There's an increasing risk that we have to have a recession in order to get inflation down," he told  Kirsten Aiken on The Business. Paul Bloxham says the unemployment rate will have to rise in order to take the heat out of the economy and put downward pressure on rising prices.

Trump Touts A Great Economy… The Voters Aren’t BUYING IT | Chuck Todd Politics Podcast

Chuck digs into why Donald Trump’s much-hyped stop in Iowa—meant to be an economic reset—falls flat with voters who are increasingly acting like the country is already in a recession. Consumer confidence has sunk to its lowest point since 2014, worse than during the pandemic, as Americans doubt job security and feel the pinch of prices despite Trump’s claims that inflation is “over.” 

Nowhere is the disconnect clearer than in Iowa, which ranks dead last in economic growth, has seen farmers hammered by tariffs, and feels uniquely damaged by Trump’s policies—creating a real possibility the state could flip blue with massive implications for control of Congress. Chuck also examines how Trump’s economic message isn’t breaking through, how he’s misplayed gun politics, and why his instinct to protect himself at all costs—throwing allies under the bus along the way—may be accelerating the political backlash.

Trump's economic policies impacting grocery prices, mortgage rates

President Trump promised to lower grocery bills. But economists and companies say that his administration's policies are hiking grocery costs.

Grocery prices last month rose at their fastest pace in three years, stoked by Trump’s tariffs, a crackdown on immigration, and extreme weather hurting food production. Prices jumped 0.6% in August from the month prior, according to the latest reading from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and they are up 2.7% from a year ago. Food prices are deeply personal to consumers, and weekly grocery bills shape their overall perceptions of the economy. More than half of Americans count grocery costs as a major stress in their lives.

US inflation is back at 3%

The cost of living got even more expensive for Americans last month, with prices rising at the fastest pace in more than year. Consumer prices rose 0.3% in September, which drove the annual rate of inflation from 2.9% to 3%, the highest it’s been since January, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data released Friday. CNN’s Matt Egan reports.  #CNN #News
title: US inflation is back at 3%

Economy Was Already Horrible. New Global Crisis Just Made It Worse.

The US lost 1.27 million jobs in 2025. Only 181,000 new jobs were created for the entire year. We haven’t seen job numbers this bad since 2010. Inflation was already out of control, housing unaffordable, grocery prices were already skyrocketing with layoffs happening every month. Now they've created a new global crisis being funded by our taxes.
